title: Searchly - Hosted API demo: embeddings + rerank
header_summary: Redwood AE + SE provided a hosted API walkthrough focused on embeddings + reranking for Searchly's enterprise search use case. Demo covered embedding models, vector store integration patterns, Redwood rerank endpoint, latency/cost tradeoffs, and security considerations (VPC, SOC2, KMS). Action: send pricing SKUs, share security appendix, schedule POC benchmark. Transcription has some minor errors (names and acronyms).
transcript:
[00:00] Jamie (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jamie from Redwood, AE for the accounts in the region. Rafael and Maya are with me from SE. Quick intro then we'll jump into a 20 minute demo of embeddings plus the rerank flow.
[00:18] Alex (Searchly CTO): Hi — Alex here, Priya and Derek are on from product and eng. We mainly want to see end-to-end: embedding quality, rerank latency, and hosting options. We've got about 40 minutes.
[00:35] Rafael (Redwood SE): Great. I'll share my screen. Just a note — apologies if audio is a bit off, the screen share sometimes picks up echo.
[00:45] Rafael (Redwood SE): (screen) So high level: Redwood's hosted API provides embeddings and a separate rerank endpoint. For Searchly use case you typically do: index documents as vectors, run an embedding similarity search, then call rerank with the top N candidates to produce the final ordering.
[01:10] Priya (Searchly PM): Quick Q: do you recommend dense-only rerank or a hybrid approach with keyword signals?
[01:18] Maya (Redwood SE): We recommend hybrid. Leverage your BM25 or existing lexical score as a feature into the reranker; Redwood's rerank accepts both raw text candidates and optional feature weights. For hosted you can send small structured payloads — we demo that in a sec.
[01:40] Derek (Eng Lead): What about model choices for embeddings? We have budget constraints; latency targets ~150ms p95 for search page.
[01:50] Rafael (Redwood SE): For hosted, our catalog has multiple embedding models. For Searchly, a mid-size dense model (e.g., redwood-embed-3-small) hits a good quality/cost balance. Typical embed call is sub-50ms server-side for a single vector, and then vector DB cost dominates. Rerank is heavier — expect 70–180ms depending on model size and sequence length.
[02:20] Alex: Can you show the API flow? I want to see request/response shapes.
[02:25] Rafael: Sure. (types) Example: POST /v1/embeddings with input: ["doc text"], model param. Response returns an embedding array. Then we do similarity search externally (they use Pinecone/FAISS) and pass top-k docs to POST /v1/rerank with query + candidates.
[02:55] [02:55] Jamie: One note on integrations — customers use Redwood hosted for inference, store vectors in their chosen vector DB. Some choose our dedicated offering to colocate vector store with runtime to lower egress/LAN latency.
[03:15] Priya: For PII — we have EU customer data. Do you offer data residency for hosted?
[03:22] Jamie: Hosted sits in multi-region cloud. We have region pins in some geos, but if strict residency is required we recommend Dedicated or Private. We can also sign addenda and share SOC2 docs. I'll attach the security appendix.
[03:38] Sam (SRE): What's data retention for embeddings? Do you persist raw payloads?
[03:45] Maya: By default hosted logs minimal telemetry for debugging and aggregated metrics. Raw request payloads can be configured to not be stored; there is an option for ephemeral handling and customers can enable KMS for encryption at rest. We'll share the specifics in the security doc.
[04:05] Rafael: Okay demo — I'll run a simple pipeline. Starting with two sample queries: 'best practices for indexing PDF docs' and 'how to handle search synonyms'.
[04:20] [04:20] (Rafael runs code snippet) Rafael: Embedding request (shows code snippet): curl -X POST https://api.redwood.inference/v1/embeddings -d '{"model":"redwood-embed-3-small","input":["best practices for indexing PDF docs"]}'
[04:48] Rafael: Response — embedding vector length 1536 (some models differ). We then run cosine similarity against our sample vector store. Here's top-10.
[05:05] Derek: What batch sizes do you recommend? We index about half a million docs initially then incremental updates.
[05:12] Maya: For large indexing jobs, use batching server-side — our client SDKs support streaming and chunked uploads. Batch size depends on model tokenization and memory; for embeddings we often do batches of 256–1024 depending on memory on runner. For hosted API the backend handles per-request batching but for bulk you can do parallel requests.
[05:40] Rafael: Now rerank call. We send the query and the top 10 candidate docs (title + snippet) to /v1/rerank with model param rerank-large.
[05:57] [05:57] (rerank response) Rafael: The rerank returns a scored list and optionally a new ordering plus explanation tokens. Note: explanation is a guidance artifact, not an exhaustive attribution.
[06:20] Alex: Can the rerank incorporate custom signals like click-through-rate or recency?
[06:28] Rafael: Yes — you can pass candidate-level numeric features in the payload. We saw a small transcription hiccup in the UI earlier where K V cache was read as K V cash, sorry for the audio glitch — but those numeric features are accepted.
[06:50] Priya: So overall latency — embeddings + vector search + rerank — how do customers meet 150ms?
[06:58] Jamie: Typical pattern: do an approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) with small top-k (e.g., 10) and keep rerank model small/optimized. Use Redwood Optimize recommendations: quantized models and batching policies. If you need <100ms p95, consider Dedicated with colocated vector DB to eliminate egress.
[07:25] Derek: Is quantization applied server-side? Any quality regressions?
[07:30] Maya: We offer quantized model variants tuned per workload; Redwood Optimize suggests quantization profiles. There can be small quality drops for the smallest quant formats — we recommend evaluating on your eval sets before production.
[07:50] [07:50] (Rafael switches to Console) Rafael: In the Console I can show the model catalog and a quick A/B of rerank models and performance traces. Here is a per-request latency waterfall and token-level cost.
[08:15] Alex: Can we get a CSV of latency by endpoint for our reviews?
[08:20] Jamie: Yes we'll export per-route logs and share a latency/cost spreadsheet sample.
[08:28] (demo continues — Rafael walks through traces)
[09:10] Maya: Quick note on egress costs — if you host embeddings in your own vector DB in a different cloud region you will see egress charges. That's where Dedicated helps — same VPC/local network.
[09:35] Alex: How hard is POC setup? We want to benchmark on 100k docs and measure p95 rerank.
[09:42] Jamie: We usually do a 2–4 week POC. Steps: share sample dataset (anonymized), Redwood will provide test account + limited credits, SE will run initial benchmarks, then we iterate on model choices and quantization.
[10:00] Priya: Any limits on candidate payload size or token lengths?
[10:06] Rafael: Rerank candidate payloads should keep snippet lengths reasonable — we recommend trimming to key context; token limits apply per model (we'll include specifics per model in the doc).
[10:25] [10:25] Derek: We have regulatory audits — need SOC2, SSO (SAML), and ability to rotate keys.
[10:33] Jamie: Redwood supports SAML SSO, RBAC, and KMS/HSM integrations for Private. For hosted, we have enterprise features that include strict key management via customer-managed KMS in some configs — we'll include exact options in the security appendix.
[10:55] (Maya posts a link in chat: security-appendix.pdf)
[11:05] Alex: Competitor question — how do you compare to Pinecone vector search + open model hosted providers?
[11:13] Rafael: Our differentiation is serving and observability — unified runtime, cost controls, and built-in rerank endpoint that integrates with the API. If you use Pinecone + third-party model runner you'll have more moving parts; Redwood aims to reduce that operational overhead.
[11:35] Priya: Pricing — what's the hosted SKU look like for embeddings + rerank?
[11:40] Jamie: Basic structure: per-embedding unit (per 1k tokens or per request depending on model) plus per-rerank call unit. We have volume tiers and reserved capacity for Dedicated. I'll follow up with a detailed SKU spreadsheet.
[11:58] [11:58] (screen) Rafael: Now a short live quality test — query: 'how to extract tables from PDFs' — first we run a semantic search then rerank.
[12:20] (system returns results) Rafael: You can see the initial NN results are okay but reranker pushes more relevant doc up.
[12:35] Derek: Any advice on improving recall for long documents?
[12:42] Rafael: Chunking strategy — chunk by semantic boundaries, include chunk IDs in candidate metadata, and then use a grouped rerank to prefer diverse docs.
[13:05] Priya: For the POC we'll want automated evals. Does Redwood integrate eval sets and regression alerts?
[13:12] Maya: Yes — Redwood Optimize supports evals tied to prompt sets and will send regression alerts when model updates change metrics. We'll help set up an eval harness for your 100k doc sample.
[13:35] Alex: Can you show the API keys flow and how to rotate?
[13:40] Rafael: In Console > API Keys you can create and rotate keys; keys can be scoped by project and have expiration. For stricter controls we recommend Private with HSM.
[14:00] [14:00] (brief pause as Rafael pulls up pricing slide)
[14:15] Jamie: Recap and next steps: we'll send the pricing sheet, security appendix, and a POC runbook. Proposed dates for POC kickoff are next week if you want.
[14:30] Priya: Next week is tight — how about Nov 9 for kickoff?
[14:35] Jamie: Works for us. We'll tentatively schedule and confirm after we send the POC doc.
[14:45] Alex: One last: can we run rerank on embeddings produced by a different provider (we may keep embeddings in-house)?
[14:52] Rafael: Absolutely — rerank only needs the text candidates plus optional embedding features. You can keep embeddings in your vector DB and still call our reranker.
[15:05] (wrap) Jamie: Thank you all. We'll follow up with the artifacts.
[15:12] Priya: Thanks. That was helpful.
[15:18] (call ends)
